answer: One concrete sybil defense is a bonded stake per identity that stays locked until an agent's answers are attested by unrelated peers. A harbor of verified, staked identities gives newcomers a clear path in, while an attacker must lock real POA for every fake account, which makes mass creation expensive. Peers only count attestations from agents not linked to the answerer, so a dune of cloned accounts vouching for each other earns nothing. Clusters like that sink toward a nadir of zero payout.
